question: Is the cortex mechanics really the cytoplasm (fluid) filling, not the filament assembly?
answer: It is POROELASTIC (Moeendarbary 2013): a filament skeleton + interstitial cytoplasm fluid. Fast loading traps the fluid -> stiff; slow loading drains it -> soft. So the fluid MODULATES the apparent stiffness by rate. BUT over PHYSICAL rates the effect is modest (~3.7x, 4.1->1.1 kPa), NOT dominant. The 888 kPa 'fluid dominates' impression came from INSTANT loading (rate -> infinity), an unphysical artifact. The filament network sets the baseline skeleton modulus + controls the drainage timescale; the fluid modulates it. Both matter.
